heading: INT. COVERED SWIMMING POOL GYM - DAWN

units.text: INT. COVERED SWIMMING POOL GYM - DAWN
An old municipal pool drained and boarded over.
A boxing ring stands where the deep end once was.
Tile walls, high windows, a faint chlorine ghost.
A cassette player sits on a folding chair.
TOMAS "THE HAMMER" IBARRA (40s, gray at the temples, hand wraps already on) shadowboxes in the ring, light as a man half his age.
He moves slowly, almost lazily, rolling his shoulders, humming along to nothing.
He taps the heavy bag as he passes it, as if saying good morning.
He stops at the ropes.
Peels the wrap from his left hand, flexes the knuckles, winces at nothing.
He sits on the stool.
Looks at the empty seats that were once pool bleachers.
He thumbs the cassette player.
It clicks.
A crowd roars on tape, then an interviewer's voice, then his own, younger and cocksure.
I'll never quit. They'll have to carry me out.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: He listens.
His smile fades by degrees.
He rewinds.
Plays it again.
I'll never quit. They'll have to carry me out.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: He rises, steps through the ropes, takes the old trophy off the shelf, and weighs it in his hand.
Then he carries it to the corner of the room where a cardboard box waits.
He sets it inside, next to a folded robe and a pair of worn gloves, and closes the flaps.
The lights above flicker on.
A side door creaks.
Footsteps click toward him across the tile, and he does not turn around.
He picks up the box, hugs it to his chest, and for the first time all morning his hands are shaking.
I'm not ready.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: The cassette reaches its end and clicks off.
In the silence, a distant bell, the fire station down the road, rings six times.
